Welcome to the Canadian Children’s Museum! Join us on a global adventure through a Mexican kitchen, an open-air market, and a cargo ship. Our Museum provides a unique educational experience, broadening children’s horizons by inviting them to explore diverse cultures. Nestled within the Canadian Museum of History in Gatineau, just minutes from downtown Ottawa, it’s the ideal family destination for a day brimming with laughter, exploration, and educational fun! The Theatre is closed for facility upgrades. A temporary theatre can be found in the Imagination in Action Gallery. Gift Shop Plan your visit Host a birthday party Canada Strong Pass The Summer 2026 Canada Strong Pass has now concluded. We hope you made the most of the program’s benefits and enjoyed discovering new cultural experiences throughout Canada. Get tickets Tickets Admission fees Save 10% when you book your tickets online ! Taxes are not included. Admission fees are subject to change without notice. Separate tickets are required for Napoleon – The Immersive Saga . Adult $25 Senior $23 (65+) Student $20 (13–17 & 18+ with student ID) Child $18 (3–12) Infant FREE (0–2) Family $68 (6 max. — up to 2 adults) Tickets can be booked in advance. Everyone visiting the Museum requires a ticket, regardless of age. The Children’s Museum is located inside the Museum of History. General admission tickets include access to the Museum of History and the Canadian Children’s Museum. Upon your arrival, go directly to the Children’s Museum entrance to have your tickets scanned. During busy times, access to the Children’s Museum is on a first-come, first-served basis. Plus icon Free admission At all times for members and volunteers** At all times for Indigenous Peoples, including First Nations, Inuit, and Métis* At all times for Canoo members (formerly Cultural Access Pass)* At all times for a single attendant accompanying a person with a disability* Every Thursday from 5 to 7 pm** Canada Day (July 1)** National Day for Truth and Reconciliation (September 30)** Remembrance Day (November 11)** Everyone visiting the Museum requires a timed ticket, regardless of their age and the day of their visit. To reserve tickets in advance, visit our online box office . *Visitors eligible for free admission can contact our Call Centre to reserve their timed ticket. **Special presentations, such as tickets for Napoleon – The Immersive Saga , excluded. Reserve your ticket Hours Canadian Children's Museum Sept. 8 to Dec. 9, 2026 Monday 9 am to 5 pm Tuesday 9 am to 5 pm Wednesday 9 am to 5 pm Thursday 9 am to 7 pm Friday 9 am to 5 pm Saturday 9 am to 5 pm Sunday 9 am to 5 pm Children’s Museum map Zoom Out Zoom In Plus icon Theatre Dress up in a costume and put on a show in a theatre inspired by ancient Greece! Plus icon Pakistani Bus Indulge your spirit of adventure on a Pakistani bus decorated in colourful suitcases. Plus icon Nigeria Explore a Nigerian house and the miniature scene inside. Plus icon Building Works Step inside the house being built and discover the many types of jobs it requires. Plus icon Mexico Explore the colourful objects to be found, floor to ceiling, in this Mexican house. Plus icon Japan Enter a Japanese house to find a festival-inspired display showcasing dolls. Plus icon Clothing Company Step inside the Clothing Company and see some critters hard at work. Plus icon India Take in the variety of animals painted on the outside of this Indian house. Plus icon Indonesia Journey through an Indonesian house and keep your eyes peeled for critters outside of it! Plus icon Pyramid Take a look at the many hieroglyphs inside the Egyptian pyramid. Plus icon Market Explore an open-air market and the worldly goods offered at each stand. Plus icon Port of Entry Learn about the many jobs and parts associated with a cargo ship on the Vegabond. View more Image gallery Share your pics! Share your travel pics with us on social media by using #CanadianChildrensMuseum or tag @CanMusHistory Pakistani Bus Port of Entry Market Bazaar Indonesia The Camel The Great Adventure Along the Nile Canadian Children’s Museum 1 / 8 Close Plus icon Frequently asked questions Plus icon What kinds of activities are there to do in the Children’s Museum? A new “look-and-find passport” activity booklet with stickers. Toys, activities, and games at destinations across the Children’s Museum, including puppet-making and a new Seek and Find activity in the Market. A daily family activity in the Studio. And more! Plus icon What activities are being offered for families at the Museum of History? Drop by the Information desk, located in the Main Lobby at the Museum of History, and pick up one or more free handouts featuring fun self-guided family activities, including: The Grand Hall… For Kids Museum Quest-ory – Canadian History Hall Stamp Find: Explore the Canadian Stamp Collection Architectural Tour Outdoor Museum Quest Plus icon Where is the Children’s Museum located? The Children’s Museum is located inside the Museum of History. Plus icon Are there washrooms located inside the Children’s Museum? Yes. There are washrooms located inside the Children’s Museum (near the Theatre), as well as washrooms located outside the Children’s Museum, near the Box Office. Accessible washrooms are located next to the boys’ and girls’ washrooms within the Children’s Museum. Plus icon Is there a nursing/diaper changing station within the Children’s Museum? Diaper changing tables are located inside both washrooms within the Children’s Museum. Breastfeeding is permitted in all public and exhibition spaces. A private nursing room is located on the lower level of the Museum of History. Plus icon Can I bring a stroller into the Children’s Museum? If visitors wish to bring a stroller, they may keep it with them or leave it at the designated stroller parking spot inside the Children’s Museum. Visitors who wish to check their strollers may do so at our complimentary coat check located in the Main Lobby. Plus icon As a person with reduced mobility, can I visit the Children’s Museum? Yes, most of the Museum is accessible for people with mobility issues. You may also be interested in Activity Leaf Suncatchers Included with admission Activity Bat hunt! Included with admission Activity Rainbow skull masks Included with admission Gift shop Timothy Bear Timothy Bear is the perfect cuddly companion and a delightful souvenir from your visit to the Children’s Museum! He is dressed in a stylish white t-shirt adorned with the iconic logo of the Children’s Museum. Price: $24.95 Buy now Metis Voyageur Arrowhead Sash Belt The ceinture fléchée , arrow sash, or arrowhead sash, is a traditional piece of French-Canadian clothing of the 19th century.
